brief.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung as most valuable Korean stock on HBM dominance; DRAM Q2 pricing up 58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ; hyperscaler capex tracking $690-725B in 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="36-3,40-2,40-3">SK Hynix surpassed Samsung Electronics in market cap on June 22, reaching 2,080.4 trillion won versus Samsung's 2,066.7 trillion won (common shares only), ending Samsung's 25-year reign.</cite> <cite index="15-1,15-15">Conventional DRAM contract prices are projected to rise 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND Flash prices are expected to jump 70-75% QoQ, driven by AI server demand and capacity reallocation to HBM.</cite> <cite index="1-1,1-8">HBM3E is expected to account for approximately two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, with HBM4 gradually gaining share as mass production ramps.</cite> <cite index="19-2,23-3">Hyperscaler AI capex is now tracking $725 billion for 2026, up from earlier estimates of $670 billion, with Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Oracle driving the bulk of spending.</cite> <cite index="30-1,30-3">TSMC's CoWoS capacity is expected to reach 115,000-140,000 wafers per month by end-2026 and approximately 170,000 wafers per month in 2027.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="36-7,39-16">SK Hynix held 61-62% of global HBM market share in mid-2025, versus Samsung's 17% and Micron's 21%.</cite> <cite index="37-2,38-21">SK Hynix shares have surged 347-348% YTD versus Samsung's 192% gain, reflecting pure-play memory exposure versus Samsung's diversified portfolio.</cite> <cite index="6-8,6-9,6-10">SK Hynix shipped HBM4E samples to major customers on June 18, with 12-layer product featuring 16Gbps per pin and 20%+ power efficiency improvement.</cite> <cite index="9-4,39-12">Samsung claims customers say 'Samsung is back' on HBM4, but Samsung only began shipping HBM4 recently and is fighting to regain share after qualification delays.</cite> Near-term relative: long SK Hynix against Samsung on HBM share, pricing power, and ADR listing catalyst (planned H2 2026). Medium-term risk: Samsung ramping HBM4 volumes, could narrow gap by late 2026. Watch for Samsung HBM4 qualification announcements at Nvidia and hyperscalers.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="17-1,17-6">Q1 2026 DRAM contract prices surged 90-95% QoQ (revised from initial 55-60% estimates), with NAND up 55-60% QoQ; Q2 2026 now projecting DRAM +58-63% QoQ and NAND +70-75% QoQ.</cite> <cite index="5-23,5-24">DRAM and NAND prices have experienced compounded increases exceeding 200% since early 2025, driven by unprecedented AI sector demand; HBM is crowding out commodity DRAM capacity with Micron noting a 3-to-1 conversion ratio between HBM and DDR5 wafer capacity.</cite> <cite index="14-8,15-7">HBM capacity for 2026 is entirely sold out, with manufacturers refusing new orders; clear shortage expected through 2026, with meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027 or 2028.</cite> Pricing has room to run through Q3-Q4 2026 given structural supply-demand imbalance, but rate of increase should decelerate from Q1-Q2 peak.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-1,1-10,7-1,7-6">HBM3E will account for approximately two-thirds (66-67%) of total HBM output in 2026, down from 87% in 2025 but still clear majority.</cite> <cite index="1-13,1-18">Goldman Sachs assessed SK hynix will maintain dominant position in HBM3/HBM3E through at least 2026 with over 50% total HBM market share; UBS predicts SK hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in HBM4 market for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="7-7,7-8,2-11">Rubin, Nvidia's next-generation AI accelerator scheduled for release in H2 2026, will use eight HBM4 stacks; AMD MI455X is also expected to pull HBM4 into volume.</cite> <cite index="7-10,7-11,7-12">Nvidia recently asked major memory suppliers whether they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026; discussions remain exploratory with no contracts signed, but have triggered internal planning around development schedules and yield targets.</cite> <cite index="3-9,3-15">Some analysts warn HBM prices could enter correction phase after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands; however, Samsung and SK hynix reportedly planned ~20% HBM3E price hikes for 2026.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ships 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers (June 18)
news_pulse.implication: First HBM4E sampling reinforces SK Hynix technology lead; 16Gbps per pin and 20%+ power efficiency improvement versus HBM4 positions company for next-gen Rubin/MI455X platforms. Material positive for margin trajectory in H2 2026-2027.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung as Korea's most valuable stock (June 22)
news_pulse.implication: Market cap flip (2,080.4 trillion won vs 2,066.7 trillion won common-only) reflects structural revaluation of pure-play memory exposure in AI era. ADR listing planned H2 2026 could trigger passive inflows and Philadelphia Semi index inclusion.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI triggers circuit breakers twice in single day; SK Hynix and Samsung both plunge 12% (June 23)
news_pulse.implication: Sharp reversal erases prior-day gains; KOSPI closed down nearly 10% at 8,203 points. Korean memory names sold off on profit-taking and concerns about valuation stretch. Micron (MU) earnings June 24 now critical test for AI memory supercycle narrative.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex guidance for 2026 revised to $725B, up from $670B estimate
news_pulse.implication: Microsoft capex guidance increased 24% to $190B, Meta up 8% to $135B, Amazon flat at $200B. Incremental $55B increase supports HBM and enterprise DRAM/SSD demand through year-end. Positive for memory pricing power and allocation dynamics.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q2 2026 DRAM +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: NAND pricing acceleration outpacing DRAM for first time in current cycle, driven by enterprise SSD demand for AI inference. Spot pricing discipline holding despite end-market PC/smartphone weakness. Suppliers prioritizing profitability over volume through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity to reach 115-140K wafers/month by end-2026, 170K in 2027
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS expansion accelerating in Tainan and Chiayi; Nvidia securing over 60% of 2026 capacity. CoPoS panel-level packaging pilot line equipment installation completed in February, mass production expected 2028-2029. Advanced packaging remains bottleneck for HBM adoption.

news_pulse.headline: CLSA: Memory chips now 52% of semiconductor revenue, up from 28% a decade ago
news_pulse.implication: Memory transition from commodity to strategic asset complete. CLSA sees valuation re-rating continuing with over 50% of Samsung/SK Hynix capacity tied to long-term agreements. Target prices: Samsung 540K won, SK Hynix 3.7M won.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia exploring 16-layer HBM delivery for Q4 2026; qualification expected before Q3
news_pulse.implication: 16-layer HBM pull-forward (likely HBM4 or HBM4E designation) raises technical bar for suppliers before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout. Samsung considering hybrid bonding for 7th-gen 16-layer HBM4E; SK Hynix developing hybrid bonding as backup while maximizing MR-MUF technology.

brief.derivatives_signal: Equity index volatility: KOSPI VIX spiked on June 23 circuit breakers; memory names whipsawed after multi-month rally. Options flow: monitor skew in Samsung/SK Hynix ADRs (SSNLF/HXSCL) and MU ahead of June 24 Micron earnings. FX: USDKRW sensitivity elevated given sharp KOSPI drawdown and foreign capital flow reversals. Watch June 24 Micron guidance closely - HBM pricing commentary and long-term agreement (LTA) volumes will set tone for July monthly settlement. Cross-asset: memory rally has driven correlation with NVDA, TSM, and hyperscaler cloud stocks; any softening in Micron outlook could trigger broad semis de-rating.
watch_for_next_3h: Stabilization or further deterioration in Korean ADR pricing (SSNLF/HXSCL) during US session following -12% KOSPI selloff
Pre-announcement commentary or data leaks ahead of Micron (MU) earnings June 24 after close - HBM pricing and LTA guidance critical for sector sentiment reset
Samsung or SK Hynix official statements regarding market cap rankings or HBM4 qualification progress with Nvidia/hyperscalers following volatility
Update on SK Hynix ADR listing timeline (H2 2026 target) - SEC filing or investor communication could provide near-term catalyst post-selloff
Further hyperscaler capex guidance revisions or AI infrastructure commentary from Microsoft, Amazon, Meta earnings follow-ups
